transcript: See, E-217 comes mostly Monday morning, after the weekend. Everyone just presses reset, reset, reset. Don't do that, you'll burn the drive. What happens is humidity. The coolant gets diluted, concentration drops, and the chips start sticking on the tool, so the spindle loads up. First thing, take the refractometer and check the coolant. It should be six to eight percent. If it's like four, top up concentrate. Then clean the chip conveyor, mostly it's jammed at the back corner. Ten mm Allen key for the cover. Takes twenty minutes. The manual says check the spindle bearings. Ninety percent of the time it's not the bearings.

extraction.title: Spindle overload after humid weekends
extraction.summary: E-217 on L-04 is usually diluted coolant and a jammed chip conveyor after a humid weekend, not the spindle bearings. Check coolant concentration before anything else.
extraction.transcriptEnglish: E-217 mostly appears on Monday mornings after the weekend. People keep pressing reset, which can burn the drive. The cause is humidity: the coolant gets diluted, its concentration drops, chips stick to the tool and the spindle loads up. First check coolant concentration with a refractometer; it should be 6-8%. If it is around 4%, top up concentrate. Then clean the chip conveyor, usually jammed at the back corner (10 mm Allen key for the cover). About twenty minutes. The manual says to check the spindle bearings, but ninety percent of the time it is not the bearings.

symptoms.label: Spindle overload alarm on Monday morning

causes.label: Chip conveyor jammed at back corner

fixes.label: Restore coolant concentration
steps: Do not keep pressing reset; repeated resets can burn the spindle drive
Check coolant concentration with a refractometer (target 6-8%)
If it reads around 4%, top up coolant concentrate and re-check
safety: Stop the spindle before reaching into the work area

fixes.label: Clear the chip conveyor
steps: Remove the chip conveyor cover with a 10 mm Allen key
Clear the jam at the back corner of the conveyor
Refit the cover and restart
safety: Lock out and tag out the machine before opening the conveyor cover

transcript: When the ram is slow and you hear a whining sound, a high whine, that is air in the system, not the pump. People order a new pump for fifty thousand rupees, no need. Lockout the press first, always, it's stored pressure. Bring the ram fully up, then bleed from the top valve slowly till the oil comes without bubbles. And one more thing. The left pressure gauge reads about ten bar high. It's been like that for years. Always trust the right one.

extraction.title: Slow ram with a high whine is air, not the pump
extraction.summary: A slow ram with a high-pitched whine on HP-02 means air in the hydraulic system. Bleed it from the top valve instead of replacing the pump, and trust the right-hand gauge.
extraction.transcriptEnglish: When the ram is slow and there is a high whining sound, that is air in the system, not the pump. People order a new pump for fifty thousand rupees unnecessarily. Lock out the press first because of stored pressure. Bring the ram fully up, then bleed slowly from the top valve until the oil comes out without bubbles. Also, the left pressure gauge reads about ten bar high and has for years; trust the right one.

fixes.label: Bleed air from the top valve
steps: Lock out the press; the system holds stored pressure
Bring the ram fully up
Open the top bleed valve slowly
Bleed until the oil comes out with no bubbles, then close the valve
Read pressure on the right-hand gauge only
safety: Lock out and tag out the press before bleeding
Stored hydraulic pressure: open the valve slowly

transcript: Short shots, parts not filling fully. In monsoon this happens a lot. The dryer timer says four hours but in rainy season you give six hours, the material is holding moisture. If drying is fine and still short shots, check heater band number three on the nozzle. It becomes loose. Tighten it only when the machine is cold, never hot, you'll strip the screw and burn your hand also.

extraction.title: Monsoon short shots: dry longer, check heater band 3
extraction.summary: Q-330 short shots on IM-07 in the rainy season come from wet material; dry for six hours instead of four. If that's fine, heater band 3 on the nozzle has come loose.
extraction.transcriptEnglish: Short shots, where parts don't fill completely, happen a lot in the monsoon. The dryer timer says four hours, but in the rainy season give it six because the material holds moisture. If drying is fine and short shots continue, check heater band number three on the nozzle; it works loose. Tighten it only when the machine is cold, never hot, or you will strip the screw and burn your hand.

fixes.label: Extend drying time to six hours
steps: In the rainy season, set the dryer to six hours instead of the default four

fixes.label: Tighten nozzle heater band 3 when cold
steps: Let the machine cool down completely
Check heater band number three on the nozzle for looseness
Tighten the band screw
safety: Only work on the heater band when the machine is cold
Isolate heater power before touching the band

manualCorrections.manualSays: Dry hygroscopic material for 4 hours at the recommended temperature.

Before changing settings, check nozzle heater band 3: it works loose. Tighten it only when the machine is cold.

transcript: C-045 means belt is drifting and the sensor trips. Young fellows turn the tracking idler too much. Only quarter turn at a time, then wait, three full rotations of the belt, then see. And before touching anything, look at the tail pulley. Most of the time it's spilled material stuck on the pulley making it uneven. Clean it with the scraper, half the time problem is gone.

extraction.title: Belt drift: clean the tail pulley before touching the idler
extraction.summary: C-045 on CV-01 is belt drift tripping the sensor. Check the tail pulley for stuck material first; only then adjust the tracking idler a quarter turn at a time.
extraction.transcriptEnglish: C-045 means the belt is drifting and the sensor trips. Young technicians over-adjust the tracking idler. Turn it only a quarter turn at a time, then wait three full belt rotations before judging. Before adjusting anything, inspect the tail pulley: usually spilled material stuck on it makes it uneven. Cleaning it with the scraper fixes the problem half the time.

causes.label: Spilled material stuck on tail pulley

fixes.label: Scrape the tail pulley clean
steps: Stop and lock out the conveyor
Inspect the tail pulley for stuck material
Scrape it clean and restart
safety: Lock out the conveyor before touching the pulley

fixes.label: Adjust the tracking idler a quarter turn at a time
steps: Turn the tracking idler a quarter turn only
Wait three full belt rotations
Re-check tracking and repeat if needed
safety: Keep hands clear of the running belt while observing

tribalTips.text: Check the tail pulley first; it fixes half the drift cases
tribalTips.quote: Most of the time it's spilled material stuck on the pulley making it uneven.

tribalTips.text: Quarter turn on the idler, then wait three rotations
tribalTips.quote: Only quarter turn at a time, then wait, three full rotations of the belt, then see.

manualCorrections.manualSays: Adjust the tracking idler until the belt runs centred.
manualCorrections.expertSays: Scrape the tail pulley clean first; that fixes half the cases. Then adjust only a quarter turn at a time and wait three belt rotations.
